proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a nonnegative integer \(r_0\), fix the supplied total order \(\triangleleft\) on \(V\), and suppose that the promised inequality
\[
 r(G,s)\leq r_0
\]
is valid.  Generate each \(R\subseteq V^{-}\) with \(|R|\leq r_0\) once in the lexicographic order induced by \(\triangleleft\), as required by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}promised\mbox{-}enumerator}\), and set \(F_R=R\cup\{s\}\).  When \(R=\varnothing\), the strict-containment requirement in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\) rejects \(F_R=\{s\}\).  For nonempty \(R\), a graph search in \(B[F_R]\) decides whether \(B[F_R]\) is connected, and a reverse directed search from \(s\) in \(D[F_R]\) decides whether every vertex of \(F_R\) has a directed path to \(s\).  Hence Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\) gives the equivalence
\[
 F_R\in\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigl(B[F_R]\text{ is connected}\bigr)
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \bigl(\forall v\in F_R,\ v\leadsto s\text{ in }D[F_R]\bigr).
\]

If this test succeeds, apply it to every \(R'\subsetneq R\).  Since every strict subset of \(F_R\) that contains \(s\) is uniquely \(R'\cup\{s\}\) for some \(R'\subsetneq R\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\) gives
\[
 R\in\mathcal C(G,s)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 F_R\in\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)
 \ \text{and}\ 
 F_{R'}\notin\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)
 \quad\text{for every }R'\subsetneq R.
\]
Thus every retained set is a clutter member and every tested clutter member is retained.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}residual\mbox{-}rank}\) and the promised inequality imply \(|R|\leq r_0\) for every \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\), so every clutter member is tested.  Candidate generation without repetition proves exact-once output, and generation according to \(\triangleleft\) proves the asserted lexicographic order.  The supplied order affects only this order of output, not the hedge or minimality tests.

Put \(n=|V|\).  There are
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{r_0}\binom{n-1}{j}=O(n^{r_0})
\]
candidates for fixed \(r_0\), at most \(2^{r_0}\) proper subsets per candidate, and each connectivity or reachability test takes polynomial time in \(n\).  This proves the time bound \(|V|^{r_0+O(1)}\).  Candidates and outputs may be streamed, and a candidate, one of its subsets, and the two graph-search workspaces all have polynomial size; hence the working space is polynomial.  At \(r_0=3\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}promise}\) supplies the promise.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) excludes residual hedges of size zero, one, or two, so it is sound to test only triples.  There are \(O(n^3)\) such triples, giving \(O(|V|^3\operatorname{poly}(|V|))\) time.

It remains to prove the scoped exact-search assertion.  Use the just-enumerated rank-three clutter and start with \(A_0=\varnothing\) and remaining cardinality budget \(j=k\).  At a node \((A_0,j)\), return \(A_0\) if it meets every enumerated residual; if it does not and \(j=0\), declare that branch infeasible.  Otherwise choose an uncovered \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\).  By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}promise}\) and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\),
\[
 |R|=3.
\]
Branch to \((A_0\cup\{v\},j-1)\) for each \(v\in R\), and return a least-cost successful answer among the branches.

We prove by induction on \(j\) that this recursion returns a least-cost feasible extension of \(A_0\) using at most \(j\) new vertices, or correctly reports that none exists.  The claim is immediate when \(j=0\).  For \(j>0\), if \(A_0\) is feasible, Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\mbox{-}rational\mbox{-}cost}\) implies that every strict extension has strictly larger cost, so returning \(A_0\) is optimal.  Otherwise the chosen \(R\) is disjoint from \(A_0\).  Every feasible extension \(A'\supseteq A_0\) must meet \(R\), and therefore contains some \(v\in R\); it consequently occurs in one of the three recursive branches.  The induction hypothesis makes each branch optimal over its extensions, and comparison of the three returned costs makes the parent optimal.  Applied at \((\varnothing,k)\), this is exactly the least-cost feasible intervention among sets of cardinality at most \(k\).

The search tree has at most
\[
 1+3+\cdots+3^k=O(3^k)
\]
nodes.  Each node performs polynomial work on a clutter of polynomial size, while sums and comparisons of positive rational costs have bit complexity polynomial in \(|V|\) and the input encoding length \(L\).  The resulting bound is \(O(3^k\operatorname{poly}(|V|,L))\).  In particular, the proof optimizes only over the explicitly supplied cardinality bound; it makes no unconstrained weighted \(3^k\) claim.

Fix the supplied total order on \(V\).  By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}promise}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}residual\mbox{-}rank}\), every \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has \(|R|\leq3\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\) writes such an \(R\) as \(F\setminus\{s\}\) for a hedge \(F\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) gives \(|F|\geq4\), hence \(|R|\geq3\).  Therefore every clutter member has size exactly three.  The final clause of that theorem also yields
\[
 R\subseteq P_s\cup T_s,
 \qquad R\cap P_s\neq\varnothing,
 \qquad R\cap T_s\neq\varnothing,
 \qquad P_s\cap T_s=\varnothing.
\]

The feasible region of Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}covering\mbox{-}lp}\) is nonempty because the vector \(y_v=1\) for all \(v\in V^{-}\) satisfies every constraint.  It is a closed subset of the compact finite-dimensional cube \([0,1]^{V^{-}}\).  Hence the linear objective attains its minimum; Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\mbox{-}lp\mbox{-}polynomial\mbox{-}time}\) additionally supplies an optimal rational solution in polynomial time after the constraints have been listed.  Fix such an optimum \(y\).

Let \(0<t<1/2\), and let \(A_t\) be the set in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\).  Suppose for contradiction that \(A_t\cap R=\varnothing\) for some \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\), and put
\[
 a=|R\cap P_s|.
\]
The preceding partition and \(|R|=3\) imply \(a\in\{1,2\}\).  Since \(R\) is missed, the two threshold definitions give the strict inequalities
\[
 y_p<t\quad(p\in R\cap P_s),
 \qquad
 y_b<\frac12-t\quad(b\in R\cap T_s).
\]
If \(a=1\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v
 <t+2\left(\frac12-t\right)
 =1-t<1.
\]
If \(a=2\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v
 <2t+\left(\frac12-t\right)
 =\frac12+t<1.
\]
Either inequality contradicts the constraint \(\sum_{v\in R}y_v\geq1\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}covering\mbox{-}lp}\).  Thus every \(A_t\) is a feasible intervention.

Let \(T\) be uniform on \((0,1/2)\).  Endpoints have probability zero.  For \(p\in P_s\), the event \(p\in A_T\) is \(T\leq y_p\), and for \(b\in T_s\), the event \(b\in A_T\) is \(T\geq1/2-y_b\).  Since \(0\leq y_v\leq1\), direct evaluation of the corresponding interval lengths gives
\[
 \Pr(p\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_p\},
 \qquad
 \Pr(b\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_b\}.
\]
No vertex outside \(P_s\cup T_s\) is selected.  Using \(P_s\cap T_s=\varnothing\), linearity of expectation, and the positivity of costs from Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\mbox{-}rational\mbox{-}cost}\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{v\in A_T}c(v)\right]
 &=\sum_{v\in P_s\cup T_s}c(v)\min\{1,2y_v\}\\
 &\leq2\sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v\\
 &=2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
 \end{aligned}
\]
For every intervention \(A\) feasible in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\), its incidence vector is feasible for the covering LP and has the same objective.  Minimizing first over fractional vectors and then over feasible interventions therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]

The membership of a vertex in \(A_t\) can change only when
\[
 t\in
 \{y_p:p\in P_s\}\cup
 \left\{\frac12-y_b:b\in T_s\right\}.
\]
After retaining only values in \((0,1/2)\), these finitely many critical values partition the interval into finitely many nonempty open cells, and \(A_t\) is constant on each cell.  The critical values have Lebesgue measure zero.  If every open cell had cost strictly greater than \(2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\), then the preceding expectation would also be strictly greater than that quantity.  Hence some cell, and therefore its rational representative evaluated by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\), satisfies
\[
 \sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)
 \leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)
 \leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]

Finally, Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}promised\mbox{-}enumeration}\), instantiated with the supplied total order on \(V\), lists every LP constraint exactly once in polynomial time under the rank-three promise.  This uses the order furnished as part of the theorem's input and introduces no additional order.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\mbox{-}lp\mbox{-}polynomial\mbox{-}time}\) solves the resulting rational LP in polynomial time.  There are at most \(2|V|\) displayed critical values, so sorting them and evaluating the rational representatives and critical values is polynomial.  The cheapest evaluated set has the claimed cost and is feasible by the argument above.

Fix the supplied total order on \(V\), and let
\[
 \mathcal C_{\leq3}=\{R\in\mathcal C(G,s):|R|\leq3\}.
\]
Apply the subset tests in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}promised\mbox{-}enumerator}\) to every \(R\subseteq V^{-}\) of size at most three, generating candidates in the lexicographic order induced by the supplied order.  The hedge test is exactly Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\), and the proper-subset test is exactly the minimality condition in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\).  Consequently the output is exactly \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\), once per member and in the asserted order.  No rank promise is used for this bounded enumeration; a promise would be needed only to conclude that no larger member exists.

Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) shows that every member of \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\) has size exactly three, lies in the disjoint union \(P_s\mathbin{\dot\cup}T_s\), and meets both parts.  Define the restricted fractional and integral values by
\[
 \operatorname{LP}_{\leq3}
 =\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v:
 y\in[0,1]^{V^{-}},\ 
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v\geq1\ \forall R\in\mathcal C_{\leq3}\right\}
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}
 =\min\left\{\sum_{v\in A}c(v):
 A\subseteq V^{-},\ A\cap R\neq\varnothing\ \forall R\in\mathcal C_{\leq3}\right\}.
\]
These are proof-local names for the relaxation obtained by omitting residuals larger than three; they do not replace Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}covering\mbox{-}lp}\) or \(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\).

Let \(y^{(3)}\) be an optimum of the restricted LP.  For every \(0<t<1/2\), apply Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\) to \(y^{(3)}\).  If a residual with one parent were missed, its fractional sum would obey
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y^{(3)}_v
 <t+2\left(\frac12-t\right)=1-t<1;
\]
if it had two parents and were missed, then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y^{(3)}_v
 <2t+\left(\frac12-t\right)=\frac12+t<1.
\]
Both alternatives contradict the restricted LP constraint.  Thus every threshold set hits \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\).  The selection-probability calculation proved in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}rounding}\), applied to this explicit family of crossing triples, yields an evaluated threshold set \(A^{\mathrm{rnd}}\) satisfying
\[
 c(A^{\mathrm{rnd}})
 :=\sum_{v\in A^{\mathrm{rnd}}}c(v)
 \leq2\operatorname{LP}_{\leq3}.
\]
Every globally feasible intervention hits \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\), so its incidence vector is feasible for the restricted LP.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\) therefore implies
\[
 \operatorname{LP}_{\leq3}\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c),
 \qquad
 c(A^{\mathrm{rnd}})\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]
This is the two-approximation side of the interface.  Alternatively, an exact optimization backend may return an integral minimizer \(A^{(3)}\) with cost \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}\); no polynomial-time claim is made for this exact restricted integer optimization.

Now verify either returned intervention \(A\) by applying Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}point\mbox{-}hedge\mbox{-}oracle}\) to
\[
 F_0=V\setminus A.
\]
Because \(A\subseteq V^{-}=V\setminus\{s\}\), one has \(s\in F_0\).  The lemma says that the alternating directed-ancestor and bidirected-component restrictions terminate in polynomial time at \(\{s\}\) exactly when no hedge is contained in \(F_0\).  Since the graph is finite, every hedge contains an inclusion-minimal hedge, so absence of a hedge in \(F_0\) is equivalent to \(A\) meeting every member of \(\mathcal C(G,s)\).  Thus a successful verification certifies global feasibility.

If \(A=A^{(3)}\) and verification succeeds, restriction of the constraint family gives \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\), while global feasibility of \(A^{(3)}\) gives the reverse comparison.  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}
 \leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)
 \leq c(A^{(3)})
 =\operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3},
\]
and the exact restricted optimum is globally exact.  If \(A=A^{\mathrm{rnd}}\) and verification succeeds, the already-proved inequality gives the certified global factor-two bound.

Suppose instead that verification fails.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}point\mbox{-}hedge\mbox{-}oracle}\) returns a hedge \(F\subseteq V\setminus A\).  For each \(v\in F\setminus\{s\}\), apply that lemma to \(F\setminus\{v\}\).  Whenever a hedge survives, replace \(F\) by the returned fixed-point hedge and restart the scan.  Each replacement strictly decreases \(|F|\).  There are at most \(|V|-1\) replacements and at most \(|V|-1\) oracle calls between replacements, so this deletion procedure is polynomial.

At termination no \(F\setminus\{v\}\) contains a hedge.  If a proper hedge \(J\subsetneq F\) nevertheless existed, choose \(v\in F\setminus J\).  Then \(J\subseteq F\setminus\{v\}\), contradicting the fixed-point oracle's declaration that this deletion contains no hedge.  Hence \(F\) is inclusion-minimal, and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\) gives
\[
 R:=F\setminus\{s\}\in\mathcal C(G,s).
\]
Moreover, \(F\subseteq V\setminus A\) gives \(A\cap R=\varnothing\).  Both the exact and rounded candidates hit every member of \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\).  Therefore \(R\notin\mathcal C_{\leq3}\), and so \(|R|>3\).  The hedge and minimality tests just described verify this residual directly, completing the optimizer-or-rank-violation interface.

Let \((G,s,c)\) be any finite simple bow-free singleton-target instance in the stated class.  Thus \(c(v)\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) for every \(v\in V^{-}\), \(r(G,s)\leq3\), and \(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\).  Choose \(R_0\in\mathcal C(G,s)\).  By Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\), there is a hedge \(F\) with \(\{s\}\subsetneq F\) and \(R_0=F\setminus\{s\}\), so \(R_0\neq\varnothing\).  Finiteness and positivity give
\[
 m_0:=\min_{v\in R_0}c(v)>0.
\]
For every vector \(y\) feasible in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}covering\mbox{-}lp}\), nonnegativity of \(y\), the constraint indexed by \(R_0\), and the definition of \(m_0\) imply
\[
 \sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v
 \geq\sum_{v\in R_0}c(v)y_v
 \geq m_0\sum_{v\in R_0}y_v
 \geq m_0>0.
\]
Consequently \(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)>0\), and the ratio in the theorem is well defined.

Equip the finite set \(V\) with a total order and supply it to Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}rounding}\).  That theorem returns a globally feasible intervention \(A_t\) such that
\[
 \sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\) minimizes over every globally feasible intervention, and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)
 \leq\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)
 \leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
Division by the strictly positive LP value proves
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)}{\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)}\leq2
\]
throughout the full positive-rational-cost class in the theorem.

For the matching lower bound, fix \(n\geq2\), equip \(K_n\) with any total order, form its private-guard expansion \(G_{K_n}\), and assign unit cost to every vertex in \(V^{-}\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) gives a finite simple bow-free singleton-target instance whose bidirected subgraph is a tree of radius at most two and whose clutter is
\[
 \mathcal C(G_{K_n},s)
 =\bigl\{\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}:e=\{u,v\}\in E(K_n)\bigr\}.
\]
Since \(E(K_n)\neq\varnothing\), the same theorem gives \(r(G_{K_n},s)=3\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)=\tau(K_n).
\]
Any set of at most \(n-2\) source vertices omits two vertices and fails to cover their edge, while all but one source vertex cover every edge.  Hence
\[
 \tau(K_n)=n-1.
\]

Set \(y_{x_u}=1/2\) for every \(u\in U\) and \(y_{z_e}=0\) for every \(e\in E(K_n)\).  Each displayed clutter constraint then has left side \(1/2+1/2+0=1\), so this vector is feasible with unit-cost objective \(n/2\).  Conversely, summing the constraint
\[
 y_{x_u}+y_{x_v}+y_{z_e}\geq1
\]
over all \(e=\{u,v\}\in E(K_n)\) counts each \(x_u\) exactly \(n-1\) times and yields
\[
 (n-1)\sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}
 +\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq\binom n2.
\]
Because \(n-1>0\), division gives
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}
 +\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq\frac n2.
\]
Since \(n\geq2\) and \(y_{z_e}\geq0\), the unit-cost objective satisfies
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}+\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq\frac n2.
\]
Thus
\[
 \operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)=\frac n2
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 {\operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 =\frac{n-1}{n/2}=2-\frac2n.
\]
For the smallest case \(n=2\), the unique constraint is checked exactly by the same calculation and the ratio is one; as \(n\to\infty\), the ratios increase to two.  These unit-cost radius-two-tree instances lie inside the full weighted class.  Hence its integrality-gap supremum is at least two, and the universal upper bound proves that it equals two.

Finally assume Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}unique\mbox{-}games}\), fix \(\epsilon>0\), and suppose for contradiction that a polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists on the narrower subclass of unit-cost instances with nonempty residual clutter, rank at most three, and a radius-two bidirected tree.  Given a finite simple source graph \(H\) with at least one edge, construct \(G_H\) and assign unit costs.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) places this instance in the narrower subclass.  If the assumed algorithm returns a feasible intervention \(A\), the polynomial-time guard-replacement map in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\) returns a vertex cover \(C_A\) satisfying
\[
 |C_A|\leq|A|.
\]
The same theorem gives \(\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H)\), and hence
\[
 |C_A|
 \leq|A|
 \leq(2-\epsilon)\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)
 =(2-\epsilon)\tau(H).
\]
For an edgeless \(H\), the empty set is an optimal vertex cover.  The supposed causal-design algorithm would therefore give a polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation for Minimum Vertex Cover on every finite simple graph, contradicting Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ugc\mbox{-}vertex\mbox{-}cover\mbox{-}hardness}\).  Thus the claimed approximation lower bound holds on the stated narrower subclass.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Given a supplied total order on \(V\) and a fixed promised rank bound \(r_0\), all inclusion-minimal residual hedges can be output exactly once, in the lexicographic order induced by the supplied order, in time \(|V|^{r_0+O(1)}\) and polynomial space. At \(r_0=3\) in the present bow-free singleton model, the runtime is \(O(|V|^3\operatorname{poly}(|V|))\). Given \(k\), branching on an uncovered residual returns the least-cost feasible intervention among sets of cardinality at most \(k\), or certifies that none exists, in \(O(3^k\operatorname{poly}(|V|,L))\), where \(L\) is the cost-encoding length.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The corrected enumerator takes a supplied total order on the finite vertex set. The current claim leaves its asserted lexicographic order unbound, so the supplied order is added as a mechanical algorithmic input without changing the graph class, completeness guarantee, or running time.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Given a supplied total order on \(V\), under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every nonempty \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size three and meets both \(P_s\) and \(T_s\). For an optimal \(y\) of the natural covering relaxation, every \(A_t\) is feasible for \(0<t<1/2\), and some breakpoint choice satisfies \(\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). Such a choice is found in polynomial time by the promised-rank enumerator using the supplied order.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Polynomial constraint generation must invoke the corrected promised enumerator with a supplied total order on the finite vertex set. This threads that input explicitly and leaves the structural, feasibility, and factor-two conclusions unchanged.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Given a supplied total order on \(V\), enumerate all minimal residual hedges of size at most three in the induced lexicographic order, optimize or two-approximate that relaxation, and verify the returned \(A\) by alternating restriction of \(G[V\setminus A]\) to directed ancestors of \(s\) and the bidirected component of \(s\). If verification succeeds, an exact relaxation optimum is globally exact and the rounded answer costs at most \(2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). If verification fails, deletion-based minimization returns a verifiable \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) with \(|R|>3\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The bounded residual enumeration now requires a supplied total order to define exact-once lexicographic output. Adding that input is the requested mechanical interface correction and does not alter either branch of the optimizer-or-violation guarantee.

proposed.statement: Given a supplied total order on \(V\), under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every nonempty \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size three and meets both \(P_s\) and \(T_s\). For an optimal \(y\) of the natural covering relaxation, every \(A_t\) is feasible for \(0<t<1/2\), and some breakpoint choice satisfies \(\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). Such a choice is found in polynomial time by the promised-rank enumerator using the supplied order.
proposed.justification: The parent-spouse crossing property improves the generic factor three for rank-three hitting set to the vertex-cover threshold two.
proposed.gap: Elahi and coauthors explicitly leave efficient MCID approximation as future work, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give only logarithmic approximation in general and exact polynomial algorithms through residual size two.
proposed.consumer: The theorem provides a deterministic warm start with an auditable factor-two guarantee for the existing ILP and WPMAX-SAT workflows.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The mechanically threaded input mentions the vertex set directly, so the theorem's free-symbol metadata must include \(V\).

prose_updates.tldr: Rank three is the first nonzero minimal residual-hedge rank for finite simple bow-free singleton-target ADMGs, and four-vertex hedges are exactly complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths. A one-private-guard expansion realizes the edge clutter of every ordered simple graph, yielding unit-cost \(\mathsf{NP}\)- and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness on radius-two bidirected trees. Under the promise \(r(G,s)\leq3\), the path classification partitions every minimal residual across target parents and spouses; after polynomial enumeration in the lexicographic order induced by a supplied total order on \(V\), this yields a deterministic weighted factor-two LP rounding algorithm. Consequently, the weighted natural-covering-LP integrality-gap supremum over all positive-rational-cost instances in the promised class with nonempty residual clutter is exactly two; unit-cost complete-graph expansions witness the lower bound, and the Khot--Regev threshold transfers under \(\mathsf{UGC}\) on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. The supplied-order promised enumerator and optimizer-or-rank-violation interface support existing exact solvers without claiming an unrestricted rank-three recognition algorithm.

project_justification.gap: The published minimum-cost intervention-design frontier jumps from polynomial solvability at residual size two to unrestricted logarithmic hardness, but it does not identify the first nonempty finite simple bow-free singleton-target rank, the exact weighted natural-LP gap at that boundary, or the approximation threshold on a graphically sparse hard subclass.
project_justification.niche: Rank-three hedge clutters are not arbitrary three-uniform clutters: every minimal residual crosses the target-parent and target-spouse partition. This structure controls every positive-rational-cost instance under the rank promise, while private guards still realize every graph edge clutter inside the narrower unit-cost class whose bidirected graph is a radius-two tree.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the four-vertex obstruction classification and exact private-guard representation, transfers objective-preserving hardness, and establishes that the weighted natural-covering-LP integrality-gap supremum is exactly two over all positive-rational-cost rank-three-promise instances with nonempty residual clutter. Given a supplied total order on \(V\), promised enumeration lists the residual constraints exactly once in induced lexicographic order before deterministic parent-spouse rounding. Complete-graph gadgets supply the matching sequence, and \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional \(2-\epsilon\) hardness holds on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. The certifying optimizer-or-rank-violation interface is provided without asserting unrestricted recognition of the rank promise.

prose_updates.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply the complete hedge obstruction used to interpret residual hitting as causal identification. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash formulate minimum-cost intervention design as minimum-weight hedge hitting, prove unrestricted hardness, and settle bounded residual size through two; their boundary is continued here at the first nonzero finite simple bow-free singleton-target rank. Elahi and coauthors replace explicit hedge enumeration by WPMAX-SAT and ILP and leave approximation algorithms open, making their RC2 and Gurobi workflow an immediate computational consumer. Nemhauser and Trotter provide the classical half-integral vertex-cover geometry that informs the argument, while the parent-spouse threshold proof here acts directly on weighted causal residuals and yields the factor-two upper bound over the full positive-rational-cost rank-three-promise class after exact-once enumeration using a supplied vertex order. Alimonti and Kann provide cubic vertex-cover \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness, and Khot and Regev provide the conditional factor-two lower bound transferred to the narrower unit-cost radius-two-bidirected-tree subclass by the exact private-guard realization. Singh's LP-gap formula motivates the complete-graph sequence witnessing the matching supremum, but no sharpening of that source result is claimed. Fernau's explicit-hypergraph branching informs only the scoped bounded-cardinality routine; neither that routine nor the supplied-order promised enumerator is presented as unrestricted rank-three recognition.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The factor-two algorithm is promise-based: polynomial enumeration is guaranteed after \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and a total order on \(V\) are supplied, but it does not recognize that promise, and a successful optimizer run is not a certificate that the rank bound holds. The order controls only deterministic lexicographic output. The \(O(3^k)\) exact-search guarantee also requires a supplied cardinality bound \(k\); it is not an unconstrained weighted parameterization by an unknown optimum cardinality. Finite-sample allocation and statistical estimation from acquired experiments remain outside this combinatorial identification-design result.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact weighted integrality-gap supremum ranges over all positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and nonempty residual clutter. Its matching sequence and the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional approximation lower bound use the narrower unit-cost private-guard subclass whose bidirected graph is a radius-two tree. General positivity-based equivalence between hedge hitting and interventional identification, source complexity theorems, and rational LP solution are imported. The promised algorithms additionally take a supplied total order on \(V\), used only to make residual output lexicographic and exact once. The complexity of recognizing rank at most three, planar bounded-degree causal realizability, rank-four realizability, finite-sample allocation, and solver speedups remain open. Weighted \(O(3^k)\) exact search is asserted only for a supplied cardinality bound.

statement_notes.justification: The proposition supplies, from a total order on \(V\) and the rank promise, the exact-once lexicographic obstruction list assumed by the LP and scopes exact weighted search to a supplied cardinality bound.
statement_notes.consumer: The supplied-order enumerator is a deterministic rank-informed front end for Akbari and coauthors' software and for Elahi and coauthors' exact solver encodings.
Given the promised rank and a supplied vertex order, the theorem provides a deterministic warm start with an auditable factor-two guarantee for the existing ILP and WPMAX-SAT workflows.

With a supplied vertex order fixing deterministic bounded enumeration, RC2 and Gurobi users receive either a certified solution guarantee or a concrete large hedge to pass to the unrestricted backend.
